clop: noun. The sound of a horse 's shod hoof striking the ground.
clot: noun. A thrombus, solidified mass of blood.
col: noun. A dip on a mountain ridge between two peaks.
color: noun. The spectral composition of visible light.
coo: noun. The murmuring sound made by a dove or pigeon.
cool: adjective. Of a mildly low temperature.
coop: noun. A basket, pen or enclosure for birds or small animals.
coot: noun. Any of various aquatic birds of the genus Fulica that are mainly black with a prominent frontal shield on the forehead.
cop: verb. To capture or arrest someone.
coplot: verb. To plot (curves, points, etc.) together.
cot: noun. A simple bed, especially one for portable or temporary purposes.
crop: noun. A plant, grown for it, or its fruits or seeds, to be harvested as food, livestock fodder, or fuel or for any other economic purpose.
loco: adverb. A direction in written or printed music to be returning to the proper pitch after having played an octave higher or lower.
loo: noun. A lavatory: a room used for urination and defecation.
loop: noun. A length of thread, line or rope that is doubled over to make an opening.
loot: noun. Synonym of booty, goods seized from an enemy by violence, particularly during the sacking of a town in war or after successful combat.
lop: verb. To cut off as the top or extreme part of anything, especially to prune a small limb off a shrub or tree, or sometimes to behead someone.
lot: noun. A large quantity or number; a great deal.
orc: noun. Any of several large, ferocious sea creatures, now especially the killer whale.
orlop: noun. The platform over the hold of a ship that makes up the fourth or lowest deck, hence in full called orlop deck, especially of a warship.
ort: noun. A fragment; a scrap of leftover food; any remainder; a piece of refuse.
plot: noun. The course of a story, comprising a series of incidents which are gradually unfolded, sometimes by unexpected means.
polo: noun. A ball game where two teams of players on horseback use long-handled mallets to propel the ball along the ground and into their opponent's goal.
pool: noun. A small and rather deep area of (usually) fresh water, as one supplied by a spring, or occurring in the course of a stream or river; a reservoir for water.
poor: adjective. With no or few possessions or money, particularly in relation to contemporaries who do have them.
port: noun. A place on the coast at which ships can shelter, or dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.
pot: noun. A flat - bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food, possibly excluding saucepans (see usage notes).
pro: noun. An advantage of something, especially when contrasted with its disadvantages (cons).
protocol: noun. The minutes, or official record, of a negotiation or transaction; especially a document drawn up officially which forms the legal basis for subsequent agreements based on it.
roc: noun. An enormous mythical bird in Eastern legend.
root: noun. The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
rot: verb. To suffer decomposition due to biological action, especially by fungi or bacteria.
rotl: noun. Alternative form of rottol: a former Middle Eastern and North African unit of weight, usually 1–5 pounds (0.5–2.5 kg).
tool: noun. Any physical device meant to ease or do a task.
top: noun. The highest or uppermost part of something.
tor: noun. A craggy outcrop of rock on the summit of a hill, created by the erosion and weathering of rock.
troop: noun. A collection of people; a number; a multitude (in general).
trop: noun. Alternative form of trope (“cantillation pattern”).
cloop: noun. A slightly hollow, percussive sound.
colport: verb. To work as a colporteur
copt: verb. simple past and past participle of cop
coto: noun. A traditional Spanish unit of length, equivalent to about 10.4 cm.
cro: noun. Synonym of bro (“a male comrade or friend”).
lor: particle. Tagged at the end of a sentence to convey a sense of resignation or inevitability.
oop: interjection. Used to acknowledge a small mistake or accident.
orlo: noun. A Spanish wind instrument, possibly a crumhorn.
oto: noun. An otocinclus (freshwater fish, genus Otocinclus).
poo: noun. Alternative spelling of pooh: an instance of saying " poo ".
poot: noun. A fart, perhaps a relatively quiet one.
porto: noun. An apéritif made from port.
potoo: noun. Any species of the family Nyctibiidae within the order Nyctibiiformes related to the nightjars (order Caprimulgiformes), and found from southern Mexico to southern Brazil.
proto: adjective. Clipping of prototypical; preceding the proper beginning of something.
troco: noun. Alternative form of trucco (“lawn billiards”).
